translation.text: These and all the others with them took wives for themselves, and each chose one for himself. They began to go in to them and join themselves to them[a]. They taught them charms and incantations, the cutting of roots, and made plants known to them[b].

footnotes.text: The opening pronoun is parenthesized and the conjunction before took is bracketed in Charles. All four printed asterisks are retained: before others and all on Charles PDF52/printed14, and before joined and incantations on PDF54/printed16. The selected joined wording is rendered as printed, not replaced by the proposed mad/raving emendation discussed in Charles printed16 note2. This is a selected-edition rendering, not certification of a reconstructed manuscript reading.

Charms and incantations distinguish the two selected nouns; other possible renderings are sorceries and spells. Cutting roots and learning about plants are kept distinct. Personally viewed Dillmann1865 columns245–246 (sorcery),363–364 (incantation),183–186 (cut/cutting),241–242 (roots),727–728 (make known),143–144 (teach) and1087–1088 (join, including sexual union).

translation.text: They conceived and gave birth to great giants, whose height was three thousand[a] cubits each[b].

footnotes.text: The actual selected numeral is ፴፻, thirty hundreds, hence three thousand. My first broad-photo ledger misread it as ፫፻; the adverse correction and personally viewed900dpi detail are preserved. Only the asterisk before giants is printed: the raised7 after and is an apparatus number, not an asterisk before height. No shorter familiar height is substituted.

Cubits follows እመት, a length measure, and the repeated preposition gives each/distributive force. Personally viewed Dillmann1865 columns727–728 (cubit),311–312 (giants),451–454 (standing/stature),885–886 (give birth),1331–1334 (conceive).

translation.text: They devoured all the produce of human labor[b], until people were unable to feed them[a].

footnotes.text: WHOLE UNIT HELD. Charles marks until with paired daggers. The first fidel of the final feeding infinitive is not certified here as ሴ versus ሲ; the current source uses a literal present-day uncertainty marker rather than silently copying or normalizing the inherited source. This does not establish a Charles lacuna. The provisional English must not be applied until the exact selected inflection is settled.

All the produce of human labor renders the metonymic labor/toil noun without asserting that people themselves were already the food in this unit. Personally viewed Dillmann1865 columns1271–1272 (labor and its produce),393–394 (feed),489–490 (eat/devour),253–256 (inability-related locator and adjacent controls). Lexical range does not resolve the held selected feeding glyph.

translation.text: They began to sin against the birds, the wild animals, the creeping things and the fish, and to devour one another’s flesh[b] and drink blood [from it][a].

footnotes.text: The ending from it is bracketed in the selected text, not a secure unmarked possessive its blood. The Ethiopic suffix is feminine singular (literally from her); its referent is not made more specific here. Square brackets preserve the edition status, not an interface footnote marker. Charles printed16 note21 regards it as a doublet of the opening then. The selected clause is retained rather than silently deleted.

Sin against also permits do wrong against; the text does not specify the precise offense against each animal group. The bird, wild-animal, creeping-thing and fish sequence is retained. Devour one another and drink are separate actions. Personally viewed Dillmann1865 columns757–758 (sin/do wrong) and489–490 (mutual devouring).

translation.text: Azazel taught human beings to make swords, knives, shields and shoulder armor. He showed them ⟦?⟧[a] and their making, bracelets, ornaments, eye paint, the beautifying of eyelids, precious and choice stones and dyes for coloring[c], [and the transformation of the world][b].

footnotes.text: WHOLE UNIT HELD. The selected phrase †ዘእምድኅሬሆሙ† is daggered as corrupt. A literal what was behind them does not securely identify its intended referent, and replacing it with metals would adopt an editorial reconstruction not authorized by this selected source alone. The literal uncertainty marker preserves the unresolved phrase. No Greek, later English or German reconstruction is adopted.

Two selected square-bracketed strings are retained in the source, as is the asterisk before from every. The final bracket is a change/transformation of the world expression; it must not be silently made an unmarked independent narrative sentence. Eye-paint source form is corrected from inherited ተጽሕሎተ to the actually printed ተኵሕሎተ, subject to independent exact review. No asterisk is printed before Azazel; the provisional first ledger description was incorrect.

Readable lexical controls were personally viewed in Dillmann1865 columns143–144 (teach),393–394 (sword),1095–1096 (armor),1225–1226 (knife),823–824 (eye paint),251–252 (beautify),427–430 (eyelid),1219–1220 (dyes),1159–1166 (making/work),889–890 (change/transformation),1419–1420 (name Azazel). These controls do not repair the central daggered phrase.

footnotes.text: The words great and are bracketed in Charles and retained as bracketed English rather than silently asserted. The initial wickedness noun and the final corruption verb bear printed asterisks, both retained in the source. No verse is omitted at the page transition.

The selected plural construction is represented as many acts of wickedness, not a single quantified substance. Went astray is distinct from corrupted. Personally viewed Dillmann1865 columns281–282 (wickedness) and329–330 (straying/error).

translation.text: Amizarak taught ⟦?⟧[a]; Armaros, the undoing of spells; Baraqiel, the observation of the stars; Kokabiel, the signs; Tamiel taught the appearance of a star; and Asderel[b] taught the course of the moon[c].

footnotes.text: WHOLE UNIT HELD. The two selected accusative forms following taught resemble agent plurals (enchanters and root-cutters), while the inherited English makes them abstract arts (enchantments and root-cutting). Personally viewed Dillmann1865 columns363–364 and183–186 support the agent nouns but do not by themselves certify this selected inflection/construction. The provisional English retains an uncertainty marker instead of choosing the familiar arts rendering without a morphological decision.

Names are read from the actual selected Ethiopic spelling, not normalized to a standard Watchers list: አሚዛራክ, አርማሮስ, በራቅያል, ኮከብኤል, ጠሚኤል, አስድርኤል. Four printed asterisks, before Armaros, Baraqiel, Tamiel and Asderel, remain in the source. My first ledger omitted the Armaros asterisk and used provisional name vowels; that ledger is not the exact source transcription.

Undoing is the opening/loosening sense of the selected verb; observation, signs, appearance and course are not all collapsed into astrology. Personally viewed Dillmann1865 columns1363–1364 (loosen/undo),299–300 (observation/appearance),731–734 (sign),865–866 (star),307–310 (running/course),241–242 (roots). These readable clauses do not remove the first-clause hold.
